title: Varna 9. The Account of Sri Mahaprabhu's Coming to the Village of Yashoda
html:
Invocation of Jagadisha; Jagadisha lives in Yashoda, serving Jagannatha; the marriage of Mahesha, who stays in his father-in-law's house; three sons are born to Jagadisha; the Lord's sannyasa at Katwa and His coming to Shantipura; the Lord remembers Jagadisha and comes to Yashoda by night together with Nityananda; Jagadisha shows Them Jagannatha; the Lord asks Duhkhini for paramanna, and a cow herself gives her milk; Nityananda asks for bhekut fish with mangoes — Jagadisha finds mangoes in the month of Pausha, and the Yamuna brings him a fish; Duhkhini, in prema, stirs the boiling paramanna with her hand, and the hand of the Lord burns; Nityananda accepts Mahesha; Jagadisha's son defiles what was prepared for the Lords, and Jagadisha asks the Lord to take away his three sons — they leave their bodies and merge into the body of Gauranga; the meal of the Lords, mahaprasada and the night kirtana; the author's signature

The ninth varna

1Glory, glory to Jagadisha, glory to the merciful one!
Be kind and show mercy to me, a sinner.

2I describe your life, being an insignificant creature:
Prabhu, mercifully complete this book.

3Bhagavatananda gave me the order in a dream;
by the power of that order I describe your lila.

4I am an ignorant sinner, I know nothing;
whatever words Bhagavata[nanda] makes me speak, those I speak.1

5Thus Jagadisha abode in Yashoda:
serving Jagannatha, he settled [there].

6Serving Jagannatha with body, words and mind,
he performs the duties of a householder according to the injunctions of the shastras.

7In this way Jagadisha lived in Yashoda.
Duhkhini said: "Get Mahesha married."

8Then Pandita Thakura pondered in his heart:
how can the marriage of his brother Mahesha be arranged?

9While he was thinking this over, some days passed;
by providence a brahmana came to Yashoda.

10That brahmana has only one daughter,
and he is anxious about her marriage.

11Coming to the Pandita, he makes a request:
"Give my daughter in marriage to your brother."

12Jagadisha first ascertained his kulinya,
and then the Prabhu accepted his words.2

13After this that brahmana, before Jagadisha,
makes a certain request with humble words:

14"Mercifully give me permission
that Mahesha may live in my house.

15As long as life remains in my body,
so long let Mahesha live in my house."

16Jagadisha gave him permission for this;
having fixed the auspicious hour, that brahmana set off for his home.

17Srila Jagadisha married off his brother;
Pandita Mahesha stayed in his father-in-law's house.

18In time three sons were born to Jagadisha;
joy arose in the mind of Duhkhini Devi.

19Thus the Prabhu remains in the householder ashrama.
Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa at Katwa,

20and together with Nityananda the Lord came to Shantipura;
coming there, the devotees met with the Lord.3

21At that very moment it arose in Mahaprabhu's heart:
"In Yashoda Jagadisha is remembering Me."

22Drawn by Jagadisha's prema, Gaurachandra,
attaining the highest bliss, says to Nityananda:

23"Listen, Shripada: taking You along with Me,
today I shall certainly go to the village of Yashoda."

24Nityananda says: "Who lives there,
to whose home You, Prabhu, will go?"

25The Lord says: "There [lives] the foremost of mahantas,
by whose prema Jagannatha Bhagavan is conquered.

26His name is known everywhere in the world:
the foremost of Vaishnavas, Sri Jagadisha Pandita.

27In My childhood I met with him;
receiving My order, he took up the service of Jagannatha.4

28By My order he settled in Yashoda;
he knew beforehand of My sannyasa.

29Therefore today I shall certainly go there;
be gracious and come there [with Me]."

30Nityananda says: "Prabhu, by Your order
I shall certainly go to Jagadisha's home."

31Saying this, the two Lords set out together
and reached Yashoda when a prahara of the night had passed.5

32Arriving, the Two went towards Jagadisha's house;
the Pandita knew of it in his heart.

33In great joy he went far out to meet [Them]
and bowed down to Both, offering many praises.

34Coming into the house, he washed the feet of Both
and brought excellent seats for [Them] to sit on.

35The Lord says: "Jagadisha, I have heard
that you brought Jagannatha and serve [Him].6

36Take Me and let Me see Him —
let My eyes today attain their purpose."

37Jagadisha says: "Prabhu, You are Jagannatha;
mercifully You have made me, a sinner, Your own."

38Placing the two Lords in front, the Pandita went [behind Them]
and quickly opened the door of the shri-mandira.

39Seeing Jagannatha, [They] offered many obeisances and praises;
in the rapture of prema the two Lords danced at length.

40Jagadisha, bringing the Two to his own house,
respectfully seated [Them] on excellent seats.

41Duhkhini Thakurani came and bowed down;
seeing the two Lords, she attained great happiness.

42With tears in her eyes the devi offers various praises;
Mahaprabhu addressed her, calling her mother:

43"Listen, mother Duhkhini," says Mahaprabhu,
"today I shall eat hot paramanna.7

44My stomach is burning with the fire of hunger;
you, mother, quickly cook paramanna."

45Hearing the Lord's words, Duhkhini Thakurani
at once became anxious in her heart:

46"Where shall I get milk so late at night?
How shall I carry out the Lord's order?"

47In her own house there is a cow;
Duhkhini quickly went to her.

48Weeping and weeping, she says: "Mother, listen,
this is my request to you:

49Mahaprabhu has come here
and has ordered: 'I shall eat paramanna.'

50Where shall I find milk so late at night?
That is why I have come to you, mother.

51If you mercifully give milk,
then I will cook paramanna for the Lord."

52Hearing this, that cow said to her:
"Today my birth as a cow has attained its purpose.

53Quickly bring a vessel and hold it to me —
as much milk as you want, that much I will give.

54Mahaprabhu will drink my milk —
what greater fortune than this could I have?"

55Hearing this, [Duhkhini] brought a vessel and held it there,
and that cow gave half a maund of milk into it.8

56Taking that milk, the devi, with a joyful heart,
went to cook for the Lord.

57Meanwhile Prabhu Nityananda, filled with great joy,
gave an order to Jagadisha:

58"I shall eat bhekut fish with mangoes;
go quickly [and make] the arrangements for it."9

59Hearing this, Jagadisha reflects in his mind:
"Where shall I get mangoes in the month of Pausha?"

60Meditating in his heart on the lotus feet of Nityananda,
he went and arrived at a mango grove.

61Holding a light, he searches every tree —
and sees: on one tree there are five gandas of mangoes.10

62Bringing them, the Pandita gave [them] to Duhkhini
and set off for the bank of the Yamuna for a fish.

63To the Yamuna he speaks humbly:
"Mother, give me one bhekut fish.

64Today Prabhu Nityananda, being most kind,
has come to my home.

65The Prabhu will eat bhekut fish —
for that reason I have come to you."

66Saying this, Jagadisha stood there
and began to recite a hymn to the Yamuna.

67At that moment the Daughter of the Sun, by a wave,
brought a fish near him and placed it on the bank.11

68Taking the fish, Jagadisha came home
and gave it to Duhkhini.

69Having given the fish, Jagadisha came to the Lords
and sat [with Them] conversing about the lilas of Krishna.

70Here Duhkhini Devi, with a joyful mind,
carefully cooks for the two Lords.

71Mahaprabhu will eat payasa —
that is why she cooks, overwhelmed by prema.

72In the rapture of prema Sri Duhkhini forgot the external world
and began to stir the paramanna with her hand.

73Meanwhile Jagadisha, before Mahaprabhu,
speaking of Krishna, is immersed in the happiness of supreme bliss.

74The Lord says: "Jagadisha, listen:
why is My hand burning?"

75Hearing this, Jagadisha became very distressed
and began to think how [the Lord] might be made well.

76Seeing him troubled, Sri Gauranga Raya
ordered: "Go and look in the kitchen.

77Then you will learn the reason for the burning of the hand;
quickly put it right, so that I may be well."

78Hearing this, Jagadisha hurriedly went there
and sees Duhkhini cooking, overwhelmed by prema.

79The Thakurani is stirring the paramanna with her hand.
Seeing [this], Jagadisha says: "What are you doing, Duhkhini?

80Why are you stirring the fiery payasa with your own hand?
Don't, don't, dear — let go of it quickly!"

81Hearing this, the devi came to external awareness
and, abashed, began to speak:

82"I was as if asleep, I was aware of nothing;
but be that as it may, my hand feels no pain."

83Jagadisha says: "Why should you feel pain?
This pain Mahaprabhu has taken upon Himself."

84Hearing this, the devi, grieved, washed her hand
and began to stir the paramanna with a stick.

85For the two Lords the cooking was done separately;
in great happiness the two Lords ate.

86Having fed [Them], Jagadisha was happy
and laid the Two down on an excellent bed.

87When the two Lords had lain down happily,
Duhkhi[ni] and Jagadisha served [Their] feet.12

88Rising in the morning, the two Lords performed Their morning duties
and, through Duhkhini's care, stayed [there] that day.

89By providence Mahesha came that day;
Prabhu Nityananda accepted him.13

90Chaitanya and Nitai are the two avatara brothers;
Jagadisha and Mahesha are sold to Them both.

91The two brothers, very joyful at heart,
served the two Lords in many ways.

92Rising in the morning, the two Lords wished to leave;
Mahesha then made every effort to keep [Them].

93Seeing Mahesha's entreaty, Gauranga and Nitai
did not leave that day and stayed there.

94Taking pains for the service of the Lords,
the two brothers gathered many kinds of foodstuffs.

95They prepared [them] in the purest vessels.
At that time Jagadisha's son came there.

96In childish restlessness he played about there in many ways
and, having chewed sugarcane, threw [it] into those foodstuffs.14

97Seeing this, Jagadisha was grieved
and, overcome with anger, began to speak:

98"A householder desires offspring,
thinking: 'A son will deliver me.'

99But [this holds] only if the son is devoted to Krishna —
then it is so; such is the word of the shastras.

Tatha hi, in the Sri Narada-pancharatra, the words of Sri Vedavyasa to Sri Shukadeva:

100He is [truly] a son who becomes a devotee of Krishna, a giver of happiness and blessing: by his mere birth he purifies, as if in play, a hundred [generations] of men.15

101But if someone's son is not a Vaishnava,
then all his dharma and all his works are in vain.

102My three sons have turned away from Gaura:
if they live, I shall have great sorrow."

103Saying this, he came to Mahaprabhu
and, clasping the Lord's feet, began to speak:

104"King Indradyumna had eighteen sons —
by Your grace You destroyed them all.16

105In the same way destroy my sons —
this is my prayer at Your feet."

106Then, through Jagadisha's anger, the three noble [sons],
leaving their bodies, merged into the body of Gauranga.17

107Duhkhini Thakurani, perceiving this,
serving Gauranga, cast off her grief.

108Hearing those words, Pandita Jagadisha,
filled with joy, danced in the rapture of prema.

109Then [they] gathered various foodstuffs,
and Duhkhini herself cooked them.

110The two Lords ate in great bliss,
and then the devotees received mahaprasada.

111Having served the Lords, Jagadisha was happy;
all night he sat and performed sankirtana of the Name.

112Placing hope in the feet of Prabhu Bhagavatananda,
Ananda Dasa tells of Jagadisha's pastimes.

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the ninth varna, called "The Account of Sri Mahaprabhu's Coming to the Village of Yashoda".

Notes

  1. «ভাগবত» (bhāgavata) — taken as a shortened name of Bhagavatananda (cf. 3); possibly also "the devotee".
  2. Kulinya (কৌলিন্য, kaulinya) — belonging to the noble lineage of kulina brahmanas, important in arranging a marriage.
  3. The Lord's sannyasa at Katwa and His stay at Shantipura in Advaita's house, where the devotees met Him — CB Madhya 28, Antya 1; CC Madhya 3. The CB and the CC do not mention a visit to Yashoda.
  4. See varna 6, note 9. Here the merging of the two Jagadishas appears in the words of the Lord Himself: He met Jagadisha in His childhood (in varna 7, the episode of the offering to Vishnu on Ekadashi, which the CB and the CC ascribe to the Jagadisha of the pair "Jagadisha and Hiranya"), and by His own order Jagadisha settled in Yashoda and took up the service of Jagannatha.
  5. A prahara is a quarter of the day or night, about three hours: that is, some three hours after nightfall.
  6. On how Jagadisha, by Jagannatha's order, carried His body from Nilachala to Yashoda on his own back, see varna 8.
  7. Paramanna, or payasa (পায়স, 71, 80) — rice cooked in milk with sugar.
  8. The maund (মন, man) — a measure of weight, about 37 kg; half a maund is about 18 kg.
  9. Bhekut (ভেকুট, bhekuṭa) — some kind of fish; possibly the bhetki (ভেটকি). In the second line the edition reads «শীঘ্র গিয়া তুমি গিয়া তার আয়োজন» — the verb has apparently dropped out; taken as "go [and make] the arrangements".
  10. Pausha — a winter month (December–January), when mango trees bear no fruit. A ganda (গণ্ডা) is a count of four: five gandas are twenty fruits.
  11. The Yamuna — so the author calls the river at Yashoda; "the Daughter of the Sun" (তপন সুতা, tapana-sutā) is an epithet of the Yamuna.
  12. The edition reads «দুঃখী জগদীশ» (duḥkhī jagadīśa); «দুঃখী» is taken as a short form of the name Duhkhini (cf. 41 «দুঃখী ঠাকুরাণী»; varna 7, note 3), not "grieving".
  13. Mahesha Pandita — an associate of Nityananda, one of the twelve gopalas (CC Adi 11); see varna 5, note 1.
  14. The edition reads «ইক্ষু চিরাইয়া» (ikṣu cirāiyā); taken as «চিবাইয়া» (cibāiyā), "having chewed"; possibly "having split". Thus what had been prepared for the Lords was defiled.
  15. The verse is corrupt in the edition: «সপুত্রাঃ কৃষ্ণ ভক্তো যো ভাবতে সুখশঙ্কর। পুনাতিপুং সাংশতকং জন্ম মাত্রেন লালয়া ॥»; taken as sa putraḥ kṛṣṇa-bhakto yo bhavet sukha-śaṅkaraḥ / punāti puṁsāṁ śatakaṁ janma-mātreṇa līlayā. The source is as given by the author, not verified.
  16. According to the Puri tradition, King Indradyumna, who built the temple of Jagannatha, asked the Lord that his line come to an end, so that none of his descendants would regard the temple as their own property. "Eighteen sons" is the author's statement.
  17. Translated as in the text. The three sons are not named; in varna 12 Jagadisha's son Ramabhadra is mentioned, into whom he infused his power (śakti). From the Gaudiya-Vaishnava standpoint this is no punishment: the devotee's sons, leaving their bodies, entered the Lord, attaining liberation and eternal service at His feet. Jagadisha's 'anger' is zeal for the purity of the offering, not mundane wrath.
